key_insight: PCA of full-field strain measurements reveals yielding signatures and early localized deformation associated with later failure in thermally exposed aluminum.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help identify plasticity onset and failure-prone regions that are difficult to distinguish in conventional strain maps.
method: Measure sequential strain fields using Digital Image Correlation during uniaxial tension.
Apply unsupervised Principal Component Analysis to extract temporal signatures and spatial deformation patterns.
Compare the second-component projection peak with 0.2% offset yield and inspect pre-transition component maps.
evidence_signal: For AA6063-T5 tested as received and after exposure to 100°C, 200°C, and 300°C, the second-component peak agreed with conventional yielding, while pre-transition PCA maps more clearly distinguished features associated with subsequent failure regions.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported alloy and loading conditions; robustness to measurement noise and broader material behavior remains to be established.
paper_title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
